underReview.title: When Parents Can Spare Time: Paid Sick Leave and Adolescent Mental Health
underReview.status: Submitted, American Journal of Health Economics
underReview.abstract: We study how state paid sick leave mandates shape adolescent mental health in the United States. Using a staggered difference in differences design with data from the National Survey of Children's Health and the Youth Risk Behavior Surveillance System, we find that access to paid sick leave raises the use of mental health care among adolescents and lowers self reported depressive symptoms.

working.title: Efficacy of Technology Aided Monitoring for Early Childhood Vaccination Coverage: Evidence from a Natural Experiment
working.abstract: We evaluate the electronic vaccination monitoring system rolled out across Punjab, Pakistan, using household survey data and a difference in differences design to ask whether digital oversight of vaccinators raised immunization coverage.

working.title: Revisiting Unilateral Divorce, Health, and Crime
working.authors: with Morgan Stockham and Anwar Assamidanov
working.abstract: We revisit the classic evidence on unilateral divorce laws using modern staggered adoption estimators, including the Goodman Bacon decomposition, doubly robust difference in differences and the Callaway and Sant'Anna estimator.
